I’ve had to juggle campaign preparation, home safety, mentoring apprentices, and applying for my own candidacy, while also helping Ingrid find the right part-time teaching or lecturing position. We compared Johnson Park’s 1:00 PM opening at Oak Hill College with other options, and it was very promising—Ingrid has thirty years of primary-school tutoring experience and prefers flexibility around that time. We’ve also reviewed the bulletin board, checked the application form, and discussed contact details and required documents.

It hasn’t been entirely smooth. I’ve had no meals or appointments to remember, and I’ve been spending a lot of time reviewing openings and comparing them. I’m also thinking about Ingrid’s water, which made me concerned, and I’m worried the application deadline is approaching. On top of that, I’ve been dealing with a frightening medical emergency: I became dangerously dehydrated, collapsed, and had to be carried to the Willow Clinic. I was terrified and even ashamed when I couldn’t find a bathroom in time, and the clinic charged me.

Despite all that, I feel hopeful. I’m grateful that Ingrid is interested in the Johnson Park opening, and I’m excited to compare the details and see what matches my qualifications and flexibility needs. I’m also beginning to question my own limits and want to be more careful about my health, food, and daily routine.

At the same time, I’ve felt emotionally stretched. Being alone, embarrassed for not washing in time, and hearing people comment on it stung. I’ve also been worried about my dehydration, and the reality of my collapse and treatment at the clinic left me shaken and deeply grateful for the help I received.

Overall, I feel proud of what I’ve accomplished and grateful for the support and opportunities I’ve encountered, but I also need to rest, recover, and be careful not to let the same pressures get to me again.

I am proud of my experience and enthusiasm for emergency response, crowd control, and community safety, which matched the opening’s priorities. I feel hopeful about the Johnson Park opening, but I also feel grateful and deeply vulnerable. I want to keep helping while taking good care of myself.
